hey, i’m shivangi :) I am building Svabotix — automating garment stitching, starting from specific sub-processes toward a world where every garment is made only when it is ordered. No overproduction. No waste. I grew up in Etawah, UP — a pretty small town, pretty conservative household. My dad, to his credit, believed in education for his daughters, so he sent me to Banasthali Vidyapith in 9th grade. That was a big deal. Etawah to Banasthali felt like a different world — swimming pools, horse riding, kathak, bharatnatyam, plays, scripts. I did everything I could get my hands on. Physics and maths clicked with me somewhere in there, and through the projects I realised knowing and building on these concepts was my passion. We lost my Chachu in 2015. He was a teacher and very close to me. Before he passed, he and my dad had talked about starting a school in our village. We made it happen in 2016. Today it educates 300+ kids and almost every girl in and around the village goes there. It’s non-profit. It’s one of my favourite things about my family. After Banasthali, my dad wanted me to do CSE from there. I wanted robotics. We had our fights. I landed at MIT-WPU, Pune — which, trust me, was no small thing to negotiate from where I come from. Studying abroad didn’t even cross my head; getting to Pune was the deal of a lifetime. College started with Vegapod, a Hyperloop team. I joined for non-tech stuff and within a week became the structures person. Chassis, aeroshell, carbon fibre composites — all in-house. We competed at European Hyperloop Week twice: Edinburgh 2023, TU Delft 2022. Top 6 globally. I also founded the Indian Hyperloop Committee to bridge industry, academia, and government. Recognised by the National Academy of Indian Railways, 2022. We also started Solclean Robotics in final year — solar panel cleaning robots. Three design iterations, concept to working prototype. I exited when I joined Airbound. Between college and Airbound, I interned at Mercedes-Benz India’s process planning team — optimised assembly lines, built a PowerApps dashboard for BEMI tracking across the production floor, developed a spot weld counting system using machine learning. Composites from Vegapod led me to Airbound. I’d first talked to Naman (founder) when it was two people in a shady workshop in Bangalore. Joining looked risky from the outside — my family and college weren’t convinced. So the timing shifted, and when he offered me a job, I said yes. Good call. I was the first dedicated R&D hire. 2.5 years of building flight-critical mechanisms, developing the composites manufacturing process from scratch, designing winglets, debugging delivery drones. Every day was something new, and I loved every bit of it. Now I’m building Svaya. We’re working on automating garment stitching. The end goal is a world where every garment is made exactly when it’s ordered — no overproduction, no waste. Ambitious? Yes. Worth it? Absolutely. If you want to talk — about hardware, composites, drones, robots, garments, or anything at all — write to me: s10.shivangi@gmail.com

Svabotix2026 – Present
Founder
Automating garment stitching — starting from specific, tractable sub-processes toward a world where every garment is produced only when it is ordered. No overproduction, no waste.
Airbound AerospaceJul 2024 – 2026
Product Development Engineer — R&D
Joined as first hardware R&D engineer — worked through design, manufacturing, composites, molding, systems and what not. From 1 drone to 100 to a complete new design, covered a lot through the journey. My favourite part was the ambiguity — I didn't know what I'd work on tomorrow because it depended on what would break today.
Solclean Robotics2023 – Jan 2025
Co-Founder
Built autonomous solar panel cleaning robots during final year at MIT-WPU. Went through 3 design iterations from concept to working prototype. Achieved up to 35% improvement in panel output efficiency in testing. Exited on joining Airbound full-time.
Vegapod Hyperloop · MIT-WPUJul 2021 – Jul 2023
Head of Aerodynamics & Structures
Designed and manufactured aeroshell and chassis for a 100 kg Hyperloop prototype (Cd < 0.15). Competed at European Hyperloop Week twice — Edinburgh 2023 and TU Delft 2022. Recognised in Top 6 teams globally, most cost-effective prototype. The goal was to make a completely sustainable prototype — from materials to manufacturing process.
Indian Hyperloop Committee2021 – 2023
Founder
Founded to bridge industry, academia, and government around hyperloop in India. Engaged IIT Delhi, IIT Bombay, COEP, and other institutions. Recognised by the National Academy of Indian Railways (2022) and awarded Nation Mover 2023.
Mercedes-Benz IndiaFeb 2024 – Jun 2024
Project Intern — Process Planning
Optimised assembly lines, built a PowerApps dashboard independently for BEMI tracking across the production floor, and developed a spot weld counting system using machine learning.
Fenss TechnologiesApr 2022 – Nov 2022
Robotics Engineering Intern
Designed and manufactured a Three-Finger Gripper for a defence research organisation.
